notes: A large change (T53: about 1,000 lines): rename of the paying principal (claude -> ai) in the open's request, the stored row, runFor and read; usage entries relabelled; segments, hops and holds with eight new member operations and a health probe; Gate 1 verdicts per entry. The rename of the open's argument shows in kinds only as added members and a widened old member, so it depends on the bound lines to be told; I expect 'bound changed' there, while the real effect on a caller still sending principalClaude is a refusal. The listing also lists private #members as entries, so expect many entries like AiRuns##gateSource, AiRuns##dispatchMember, AiRuns##afterStop, AiRuns.#flagOnly as new, and AiRuns##accountServing, AiRuns##accountFor, AiRuns##aiRunDispatch as changed; I have not listed those, since no user can reach them. dispatchMemberRun's parameter changes from a destructuring pattern to `args`; the tool may read that as a parameter name change. partAdmitted's and verificationRecord's behaviour changed (Gate 1, flag only) with no kind change. UsageEntry's change also reaches op:airuntick's req.

Only the private #useCheck changed (a fourth, optional parameter `served`, passed on to ai-use's useCheck). No comment needed to change. The listing lists private members, so the tool may show AiRuns##useCheck as 'accepts more' (tells nobody); no user can call it.

notes: F4 and F5. The real change inserted ANSWER_MARKS, answerKeyMarks and a private recallFit between hiddenRuns' JSDoc and hiddenRuns itself, so in the real code hiddenRuns' prose now sits on ANSWER_MARKS. The carry put my @param/@returns/@bound for hiddenRuns in that conflict; I resolved it by keeping the real layout and writing a second JSDoc directly above hiddenRuns with the same tags, so hiddenRuns' entry should be unchanged. If the tool reads the first block's prose as ANSWER_MARKS' comment, no kind is involved. pathReadyRead's no-pair case is now a cascade read: accepts more in effect, but my kinds already accepted both absent, so only the bound line shows it. The expected 'hands back differently' on PathReadyAnswer is a comment-text change only and I expect the tool to report none for it.

Only a test was added (notice-membership-1030: membership's isAdministrator now also reads member:<id>; ai-runs passes the bare id, so its answer is unchanged). No source change, no comment change. The change is the provider's answer to a notice it received, so the listing of ai-runs cannot change.
